ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Patient noticed new, painless swelling over the left elbow ≈1 week ago; no trauma, food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Gradual appearance; stable over the week; mild warmth; minimal tenderness only adjacent to tip; full range of motion; no fever or systemic symptoms.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat tightness/closure, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: First episode; no prior elbow swelling, no ED visits, no injections given.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Peanuts (food).  
  • Drug allergies: None reported.  
  • Current meds: None prior to visit; advised to start ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food (new).
- Social context: Works at a desk job; runs 2–3 ×/week; appears able to self-care; no mention of caregiver presence.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: Localized swelling over olecranon of left elbow; skin slightly warm; dry skin on tip noted; no marked erythema described.
- Airway/breathing: Normal; no stridor or increased work of breathing observed/reported.
- Mental status and associated features: Alert, well-appearing.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Likely aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis of the left elbow.
  Evidence: Localized, mildly warm swelling for 1 week, minimal pain, preserved function, no systemic signs.
- Differential diagnosis (from DDx consistent with transcript):
  1. Aseptic olecranon bursitis – classic presentation; highest likelihood.
  2. Septic olecranon bursitis – considered because of warmth/tenderness; no systemic or progressive local signs currently.
  3. Gouty olecranon bursitis – less likely; middle-aged male; no prior gout history; urate level ordered.
- ENT pathology not suspected; template requirement acknowledged (conflict noted).

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Start ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; discontinue if heartburn or GI upset.
- Diagnostics:
  • Blood tests: CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate, ± additional inflammatory markers; form to be mailed to patient.
- Follow-up:
  • Arrange review (video or in-person) ≈1 week after labs available to assess clinical course and review results.
  • Patient instructed to contact service sooner if swelling becomes very red, increasingly painful, redness spreads, or systemic symptoms (fever, malaise) develop—would warrant urgent evaluation for possible septic bursitis.
- Patient education:
  • Explained benign nature of current findings and expected course.
  • Advised on elbow protection and to avoid prolonged pressure.
  • Confirmed understanding; patient agreed with plan.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Objective vitals; precise measurement of swelling; full musculoskeletal ROS; ENT-specific airway assessment not required but template expects it; auto-injector availability for peanut allergy not discussed.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None significant; only mismatch with ENT-focused template (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional conversational filler; no inaudible segments.
